title: intent — what a session means to do, declared before it touches files
description:
The one field written BEFORE the work. A session's opening move is one sentence of what it means to do and, when 'done' is honestly a command, that command as a discharge test (`done_when`). Declaring closes pre-planning: it is the exit of the divergent stance, so it is not written while still diverging. PROSPECTIVE, so it carries a lease (lease.json rides flat): `expires` and `scope` are required beside `done_when`.

Read back at handoff as MET (the predicate holds) / UNMET (it fails) / UNARMED (statement only) / ERROR (instrument silent) — surfaced, never enforced; a session that declared nothing is ABSENT, which is 'no probe', not 'no intent'. Re-declaring is allowed and RECORDED: a second declaration with a different statement pushes the old one onto `superseded` with the reason rather than overwriting it, because the drift is the record, not noise. Never rewritten at handoff time to fit the outcome.

Writer today: hololoom_mcp/tools/session_intent.py into the live scratchpad, copied verbatim into the archive. shed's `declare` verb (not yet shipped) writes the same shape; this file is the contract both meet.

statement.description: One sentence — what this session means to do.

declared_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC. When it was declared; must precede the first file edit to count as intent rather than reconstruction.

sid8.description: Who declared it — first 8 of the session id.

superseded.description: Earlier statements this declaration replaced, oldest first. Kept, never dropped.
